title: Nebular Harvest
caption: The Raspberry Nebula, LBN 867, imaged by the Nicholas U. Mayall 4-meter Telescope
credit: KPNO/NOIRLab/NSD/AURA/T.A. Rector (University of Alaska Anchorage/NSF NOIRLab) · Image processing: T.A. Rector (University of Alaska Anchorage/NSF NOIRLab), M. Zamani (NSF NOIRLab) & D. de Martin (NSF NOIRLab)

recognition.text: NOIRLab Image of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: A characteristic red bloom of glowing gas marks this image of LBN 867, nicknamed the Raspberry Nebula, in the constellation Orion. The star HD 34989 shines prominently near the centre, wrapped in a subtle bluish glow.

Despite the nickname, the nebula is layered more like an onion than a raspberry, combining three objects in one. The red bloom is an emission nebula, glowing because light from HD 34989 ionizes its hydrogen gas. HD 34989 itself is a main sequence star; prominent as it looks here, from Earth it appears only about as bright as the planet Uranus.

The third object is easy to miss. The faint bluish glow around the star is the reflection nebula vdB 38, where nearby interstellar dust bounces the star's blue-white light toward us. The image was captured by the Nicholas U. Mayall 4-meter Telescope fitted with the Mosaic-3 detector, at Kitt Peak National Observatory, part of NSF NOIRLab.

understand.summary: Taken with the Mosaic-3 camera on the NSF Nicholas U. Mayall 4-meter Telescope through g, I and hydrogen-alpha filters; the colour mapping isn't published.
filters: 475 nm · Optical G (NSF Nicholas U. Mayall 4-meter Telescope Mosaic-3)

understand.eye: The hydrogen-alpha filter highlights the red glow of ionized hydrogen, and long exposures bring out the faint blue reflection nebula the eye would miss.

explore: Main sequence stars are those steadily fusing hydrogen in their cores, the long, stable stage of a star's life that the Sun is in today. The credit and image processing are by T.A. Rector of the University of Alaska Anchorage, with M. Zamani and D. de Martin of NSF NOIRLab.
